text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-Shipping company Leif Hoegh & Co could lose as much as 30 million crowns following the bankruptcy of brokerage Noka Securities. The shipper had a large amount of shares deposited with Noka.
-Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil) has decided to demerge the Statoil Shipping & Maritime Technology business area and form a new partnership with the Rasmussen group of Kristiansand.
-Conglomerate Rieber & Soen is strengthening its position in Eastern Europe by buying Czech food producers Emarko and Bask.

-A mathematical model by researchers at Statistics Norway indicates that a break up of the oil producers' group, the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, could lead to a reduction in Norway's oil wealth by 70 percent in the long term.

-A majority of parliament's financial committee wants to change the tax laws in order to reduce taxes for supplyships and tugboats. According to the Finance Ministry such boats are not under the same favourable rules as the shipping industry in general.
